Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be pairwise comaximal ideals, where $r\ge1$. Then the canonical map
$$ R\longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i,\qquad x\longmapsto(x+I_1,\ldots,x+I_r) $$
is surjective, its kernel is $\bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i$, and
$$ \bigcap_{i=1}^r I_i=\prod_{i=1}^r I_i. $$
Equivalently,
$$ R/\prod_{i=1}^r I_i\cong\prod_{i=1}^r R/I_i. $$

derivations.claim: **The projectors exist and are polynomials in the $x_r$.** Since the $x_r$ commute pairwise, the subalgebra they generate is the image of $\mathbb C[t_1,\dots,t_d]$, and the relation $(x_r-m_1)\cdots(x_r-m_l)=0$ holds for every $r$. Write $\{a_1<\cdots<a_s\}$ for the distinct values among $m_1,\dots,m_l$ with multiplicities $\mu_u\ge1$, so that $\prod_{u=1}^{s}(t-a_u)^{\mu_u}=\prod_{j=1}^{l}(t-m_j)$. The ideals $(t-a_u)^{\mu_u}$ of $\mathbb C[t]$ are pairwise comaximal, so [F5] applied to $R=\mathbb C[t]$ gives polynomials $E_u(t)\in\mathbb C[t]$ with $E_u\equiv1\bmod (t-a_u)^{\mu_u}$ and $E_u\equiv0\bmod (t-a_v)^{\mu_v}$ for $v\ne u$. Extend to all integers by $E_j:=E_u$ for $j=a_u$ and $E_j:=0$ for $j\notin\{a_1,\dots,a_s\}$. Then the $E_j(x_r)$ are mutually orthogonal idempotents of the commutative algebra $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ with $\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}E_j(x_r)=1$, and comparison with the defining relation shows that $E_u(x_r)$ projects onto the generalized eigenspace of $x_r$ at $a_u$. Putting $e(i):=\prod_{r=1}^{d}E_{i_r}(x_r)$ for $i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in\mathbb Z^d$ gives mutually orthogonal idempotents in $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ with $\sum_i e(i)=1$; only finitely many are nonzero because each $x_r$ has at most $s$ generalized eigenvalues. For a finite-dimensional $H_d(m)$-module $M$ the commuting endomorphisms $x_r$ are simultaneously triangularizable on each generalized joint eigenspace, so $e(i)M=\{v\in M:(x_r-i_r)^Nv=0\ \text{for all }r\text{ and }N\gg0\}$; this is the generalized weight space decomposition of $M$.

**The stable realization and the centre comparison.** Assume first that the data lie in an admissible stable realization; then $H_d(m)\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$ for the prinjective detector $T_\alpha$ of the genuine parabolic block $\mathcal O_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], by [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]]. Choose a finite projective generator $Q$ of $\mathcal O_\alpha$ with $T_\alpha$ a direct summand, and put $A:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$ and $H:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}=eAe$, where $e$ is the idempotent of the summand $T_\alpha\subseteq Q$. Only finitely many isomorphism classes of indecomposable projectives occur, so this is a finite selection. Full faithfulness of the Schur quotient on all projectives ([[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]) gives an algebra isomorphism $A\cong\operatorname{End}_H(\pi Q)^{op}$, where $\pi$ is the quotient functor onto the modules over $H$. Since $Q$ contains a representative of every projective, $\pi Q$ contains the image of every projective of $\mathcal O_\alpha$; as a projective generator of $H\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, the module $\pi Q$ is a progenerator, and the centre of the endomorphism ring of a progenerator is Morita invariant: $Z(A)\cong Z(H)$. Concretely, a central $h\in H$ acts on $\pi Q$ by left multiplication, which is a central $H$-linear endomorphism and therefore, by full faithfulness on the projective $Q$, is the image of a unique central element of $A$; restricting a central element of $A$ to $eAe=H$ inverts this correspondence, the composite $Z(H)\to Z(A)\to Z(H)$ being the identity because it is the identity on $\pi T_\alpha=H$, and the other composite being the identity because for every indecomposable summand $Q'\subseteq Q$ the module $\pi Q'$ is generated by its images under $H$-linear maps from the summands of $\pi T_\alpha$ (a projective cover is generated by any of its simple quotients and $\pi Q'$ either is such a cover or is a non-projective image whose generators are reached from the covers by quotient maps), so agreement on $\pi T_\alpha$ forces agreement on $\pi Q'$ and hence on $\pi Q$.

**Content idempotents are central.** For fixed $\alpha$ the set $I_\alpha$ is the set of all orderings of one multiset of entries of $I$ of size $d$, hence a single orbit of the position permutation action of $S_d$ on $I^d$; it is finite. The element $e_\alpha=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}e(i)$ is therefore the symmetrization over that orbit of the monomial $\prod_{r=1}^{d}E_{i_r}(x_r)$: permuting the variables $x_1,\dots,x_d$ permutes the orderings in $I_\alpha$, so $e_\alpha$ is a symmetric polynomial in $x_1,\dots,x_d$.

**A single linkage block has no split central idempotent.** $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a single linkage block by [[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]: it admits no decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal factors. A central idempotent $f=f^2\ne0$ of $A$ with $f\ne1$ would split the projective generator $Q=Qf\oplus Q(1-f)$ into two nonzero summands whose Hom-spaces in both directions vanish, because every morphism between them is annihilated by composing with $f$ on either side in the two possible orders; this exhibits $\mathcal O_\alpha$ as the product of the two nonzero full subcategories generated by these summands, contradicting single-linkage. Hence $Z(A)$ has no nontrivial idempotent, and by step 1.2 the same holds for $Z(H)=Z(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$: the stable content component is a single block.

**Symmetric polynomials in the $x_r$ are central.** It suffices to show that the elementary symmetric functions in the $x_r$ are fixed by conjugation with each basic transposition $s_r$, since these generate the symmetric polynomials and commute with all $x_i$ with $i\notin\{r,r+1\}$. The defining cross relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ and $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$; multiplying the first by $s_r$ on the left yields $s_rx_{r+1}s_r=x_r+s_r$, and the second yields $s_rx_rs_r=x_{r+1}-s_r$. Consequently $s_r(x_r+x_{r+1})s_r=x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $s_r(x_rx_{r+1})s_r=(x_{r+1}-s_r)(x_r+s_r)=x_rx_{r+1}$, so the two elementary generators in the pair $\{x_r,x_{r+1}\}$ are fixed, and $s_r^2=1$ makes the same true for every polynomial in them; together with the commuting generators this fixes every symmetric polynomial. Comparing with step 2.1, $e_\alpha$ commutes with every $x_i$ and every $s_r$, hence is central in $H_d(m)$.

**Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set and fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations to be performed. Choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and an upper endpoint $r$ so that every charge $m_j$ lies in the letter alphabet $[k,r+1]$ and every simple-root support occurring in the list lies in $[k,r]$; enlarge an auxiliary stable realization only in the direction of the stable range, so that the added bottom rows of every tableau are forced to keep the ground entry in every column and every added top entry is absent. By the actual double-cut/common-tail compatibility and the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] and [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], the $I$-supported content component $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the same finite-dimensional algebra as the corresponding content component of the stable realization, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, the same residue projectors and the same residue maps; no whole-degree equality is used. Applying step 2.2 to that common component proves (b) for arbitrary consecutive $I$.

**Nonzeroness is open.** Centrality neither makes $e_\alpha$ primitive nor excludes $e_\alpha=0$; both questions are settled by steps 2.2 and 3.2 using the stable realization, whose hypotheses are the ones declared in the Given.

**Level zero and the vanishing witness.** At level $0$ the cyclotomic polynomial is the empty product $1$, so $H_d(m)=0$ for $d>0$ and only $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ remains; this is the convention of (2). For the witness, $I=\{0\}$, level $1$, charge $(0)$, $d=2$: the level-one presentation gives $x_1=0$ and $x_2=s_1$, so $H_2(0)=\mathbb C[S_2]$ with eigenvalues $\pm1$ for $x_2$; hence $E_0(x_2)=0$, $e(0,0)=0$, and the supported component $H^\Lambda_{2\alpha_0}=e_{(0,0)}H_2(0)$ is $0$, while $H_2(0)\ne0$. This completes the proof of the two claims (b) and the level-$0$ convention; the exactness and biadjointness clauses of (4) are the declared supplier statements of [[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]], not reproved here.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be essentially small abelian categories and let
$\mathcal D,\mathcal D'$ be essentially small additive categories. For any
abelian group $H$, every function
$\chi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal C)\to H$ satisfying
$\chi(Y)=\chi(X)+\chi(Z)$ for every short exact sequence
$0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\chi\colon G_0(\mathcal C)\to H$ with
$\overline\chi([X])=\chi(X)$. Every function
$\psi\colon\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)\to H$ satisfying
$\psi(X\oplus Y)=\psi(X)+\psi(Y)$ factors uniquely as a homomorphism
$\overline\psi\colon K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathcal D)\to H$ with
$\overline\psi([X])=\psi(X)$. Here $\operatorname{Iso}$ is the set of
isomorphism classes, so these are class functions.

An exact functor between essentially small abelian categories induces a
homomorphism on $G_0$, and an additive functor between essentially small
additive categories induces a homomorphism on split $K_0$. These assignments
preserve identities and composition. Naturally isomorphic exact functors, or
naturally isomorphic additive functors, induce equal homomorphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $K(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(K(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(K(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]].

**The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]].

**The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

**The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$.

**The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a generalized-standard composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):K(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):K(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i).

**Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is generated by the ground vector $D_{A_\Lambda}$ over $\mathbb Q$ and is identified with the form-dual family by the same theorem. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices.

**Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ on $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]] are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2], and they intertwine with the category-O residue functors through the Schur quotient: $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$, compatibly with residue projectors and dualities, by [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]]. On the category-O side the induced $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley operators, and a residue translate of a simple either vanishes along an absent crystal edge or is a self-dual indecomposable whose simple head and socle is the translated label, by [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]]; ungraded at parameter $1$ these are exactly the operators $e_i,f_i$ on the Fock module, so under $\Phi$ the residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators, giving the first half of (ii).

**Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with no further costandard vectors, standard lattice or residue operators. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v).

**Crystal reachability.** By step 3.1 a residue translate of a simple is zero or a self-dual indecomposable with simple head and socle the crystal-translated label, and the residue operators are the Fock Chevalley operators; starting from the ground simple $D(A_\Lambda)$ and following any reduced crystal word to $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, each intermediate translate is nonzero (the corresponding crystal edge exists along the word) and exactness of the residue functors makes the final simple a composition factor of the word applied to the ground. Conversely, a simple composition factor of any residue word applied to the ground lies in the highest crystal component, which is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ because the highest weight Fock module is generated by the ground monomial and its standard monomials are indexed by $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ ([[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]). This proves (iv).

**Rational ground cyclicity.** Over $\mathbb Q$ the element $D_{A_\Lambda}$ is a highest weight vector for the integrable action of step 3.1, and $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$ is irreducible: it is the dual of the irreducible highest weight module, and the span over $\mathbb Q$ of the orbit of the ground vector is a nonzero submodule, hence all of $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$. Thus the ground class generates $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, proving the rational clause of (iii).

**The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$ and the costandard basis $(D_{00},D_{01},D_{11})$ of the three nonzero content classes. The residue operators act by $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$, $fD_{11}=0$ and $eD_{00}=0$, $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$; this is the degree-one block $B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ sitting in degree two as a corner together with the two-dimensional block $M_2(\mathbb C)$, where $D_{11}$ is two-dimensional with $x\mapsto0$ on the simple and the second divided power $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$, $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. The lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}:=\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ contains the ground, is stable under $f,e$ and their divided powers and under the toral operators, and does not contain $D_{01}$: any element whose $D_{01}$-coordinate is odd lies outside, and the operators multiply $D_{01}$-coefficients by even integers. Hence $L_{\mathbb Z}$ is a proper integral costandard submodule containing the ground vector, so the costandard lattice is not ground cyclic over $\mathbb Z$ even under divided powers, while dividing by $2$ over $\mathbb Q$ restores cyclicity; this proves the failure clause of (iii) and, with step 5.1, the first half of (v).

**Conclusion.** Step 2.1 identifies $G_0$ with the full integral costandard lattice and step 2.2 computes the Specht classes, proving (i); step 2.3 gives the divided-power integral forms and step 3.1 identifies the residue operators with the Chevalley operators, proving (ii); step 5.1 proves rational ground cyclicity, step 2.3 proves integral ground generation of the standard lattice and step 6.1 exhibits the index-two failure of integral costandard cyclicity, proving (iii) and its sharpness; step 4.1 proves the crystal reachability statement (iv); and step 3.2 (level zero) together with steps 5.1 and 6.1 separates the rational-cyclicity and categorical reachability conclusions from integral costandard cyclicity, as asserted in (v). No step identifies $\{D_A\}$ with the standard divided-power lattice, and no integral costandard generation is used.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital algebra over a field $k$. Write
$S_1,\ldots,S_t$ for representatives of the isomorphism classes of simple
left $A$-modules, and choose a finite-dimensional projective cover
$q_i\colon P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ for each $i$. Then the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective left $A$-modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]) is the free abelian
group with basis $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$. In particular, each selected cover is
indecomposable, the $P_i$ are pairwise nonisomorphic, and every finite
dimensional projective is a finite direct sum of them. This result makes no
claim that the Cartan map to the short-exact-sequence group $G_0(A)$ is
invertible.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative $k$-algebra. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent all isomorphism classes of simple left $A$-modules, and let $q_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite-dimensional projective covers. Then $[P_1],\ldots,[P_t]$ and $[S_1],\ldots,[S_t]$ are bases of $K_0(A)$ and $G_0(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_A=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_A(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ In particular, if $\operatorname{End}_A(S_i)=k$ for every $i$, these bases are dual.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra, let $S_1,\ldots,S_t$ represent the graded-simple shift orbits and let $p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$ be finite graded projective covers. Here graded-simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero graded submodule. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. Neither pairing statement asserts unimodularity of the projective-to-module Cartan map or of a projective/projective Cartan matrix. No axiom of choice is assumed or used.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital $k$-algebra. For a
finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and finite-dimensional left
$A$-module $M$, define the object-level value

$$h(P,M):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,M).$$

If $A$ is $\mathbb Z$-graded and $P,M$ are finite-dimensional graded left $A$-modules,
with $P$ projective in the degree-zero graded category, define

$$h_{\mathrm{gr}}(P,M):=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}v^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M),$$

where $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M)$ consists of $A$-linear maps sending each
$P_i$ into $M_{i+d}$. These are candidate values on object isomorphism
classes; no descent to pairings on $K_0\times G_0$ is asserted here.

Let $k$ be a field and let $A,B$ be finite-dimensional unital associative
$k$-algebras. Write $A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$ and
$B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$ for their categories of finite-dimensional
left modules. Let
$F:A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}\to B\text{-}\mathrm{mod}_{\mathrm{fd}}$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $\lambda'$ be the

([[def-sign-representation-and-restriction-of-a-representation]]), and let
$$S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$$
be the tensor product of $F[S_n]$-modules with the diagonal action
$\sigma\cdot(x\otimes w):=(\sigma\cdot x)\otimes(\sigma\cdot w)$, a
finite-dimensional $F[S_n]$-module

   $\theta:M^{\lambda'}_F\to S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}$ with

2. $\theta$ is surjective and
   $\ker\theta=(S^{\lambda'}_F)^\perp$.

   $$M^{\lambda'}_F/(S^{\lambda'}_F)^\perp\cong S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}, \qquad\text{hence}\qquad S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\cong (S^{\lambda'}_F)^*,$$
   the second being the composite with $x\mapsto\beta_F(x,\cdot)|_{S^{\lambda'}_F}$.

No nondegeneracy of $\beta_F$ restricted to $S^{\lambda'}_F$ is assumed, and

derivations.claim: **The sign automorphism.** The assignments $\sigma(s_r)=-s_r$ and $\sigma(x_r)=-x_r$ respect the defining relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: involution and braid relations hold for the $s_r$ and the $x_r$ commute, and the cross relation $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$ is preserved because both sides change sign in the $x$-variable and $1$ is fixed, while $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ is preserved the same way. Hence $\sigma$ is an algebra automorphism of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra; it maps the polynomial idempotent $e(i)$ to $e(-i)$ and therefore the block idempotent $e_\alpha$ of $H_d(m)$ to the block idempotent $e_{\alpha^t}$ of $H_d(m^t)$, giving an isomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong H^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$ that intertwines the tower inclusion and the residue projectors $u_{\alpha,i}$ with $u_{\alpha^t,-i}$; twisting modules by $\sigma$ gives exact functors that interchange residue $i$ with residue $-i$ and commute with the duality $\circledast$ (which is defined by the $x_r$- and $s_r$-fixed anti-automorphism and is therefore $\sigma$-stable).

**The transpose of multipartitions.** Reversing the $l$ components of an $l$-multipartition and transposing each component is an involution $\lambda\mapsto\lambda^t$ that maps the multipartitions of the Fock shape $\Lambda$ of weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ to those of shape $\Lambda^t$ of weight $\Lambda^t-\alpha^t$; on tableaux it induces the tableau bijection of the source, and row-versus-column inequalities interchange, so it restricts to a bijection $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$. This is the combinatorial part of [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]] and [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], specialized to the multipartition dictionary of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]].

**Full faithfulness on all projectives and tiltings.** In the admissible stable realization the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ is fully faithful on ALL category-O projectives and on all tilting objects, the endomorphism isomorphism identifies the Hecke image algebra with the endomorphism algebra of the prinjective detector, and the category-O tilting objects are classified with a standard flag, by [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] and [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]; the Young and signed-Young images are the ones of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]].

**Longest-shuffle induction duality.** Let $P$ be the affine Young subalgebra with original block sizes and $Q$ the reversed block subalgebra. Affine PBW on the right gives $H_d=\bigoplus_{u\in U}uP$, where $U$ consists of minimal right coset representatives. Its unique longest representative $r$ reverses the blocks, preserving their internal orders; its length is the number of cross-block pairs. Let $\theta:Q\to P$ relabel positions by $r^{-1}$ and let $E(\sum up_u)=p_r$. Then $E$ is right $P$-linear and $E(qh)=\theta(q)E(h)$. Indeed straightening $x_ju$ gives $ux_{u^{-1}j}$ plus shorter-permutation terms, which cannot reach the longest coset, and an internal $Q$ reflection preserves that coset with $s_jr=r\theta(s_j)$. For finite $P$-module $M$, give $M^*$ its generator-fixing dual action and transport it to $Q$ through $\theta$. The pairing $\langle a\otimes m,b\otimes\varphi\rangle=\varphi(E(b^*a)m)$ is balanced by these two identities and is contravariant.

Minimal representatives $v$ for $H_d/Q$ satisfy $vr\in U$; $E(v^{-1}u)$ is one precisely when $u=vr$ and zero otherwise. Thus the pairing matrix is a permutation matrix tensored with the ordinary perfect pairing, proving that the dual of induction is the reverse-block induction of the dual.

**The correctly normalized exterior quotient.** Choose a sufficiently low finite cut $k$, put $q_i=m_i+1-k$, $n=q_1$ and $c=n+k-1$. The ordinary parabolic ground has scalar $q_1+\cdots+q_{i-1}+m_i$, obtained from the head character $-\rho_i=\sum_{j\le i}q_j-n$ plus $c$. The finite-W tail shift is a different embedding convention and is not substituted for this character; the transported roots are nevertheless exactly $m_i=c+q_i-n$. For the transposed component partitions $\nu^{(i)}=(\lambda^{(i)})^{\mathsf T}$ form the exterior suffix module $D=\mathbb C_c\otimes\bigotimes_{i=l}^1\bigwedge^{\nu^{(i)}}(V/V_{i-1})$. Its tensor quotient $q:U=\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}\to D$ is parabolic-linear and hence finite-W-linear. Select $d$ distinct longest row names with idempotent $e_S$ and cyclic rightmost-row tensor $w$; regular evaluation identifies $H\to e_SU$, $b\mapsto wb$, with left corner action $a(wb)=w(ab)$. Therefore $K=\ker(q\,\mathrm{reg})$ is a LEFT ideal; no right-Hecke linearity of the exterior quotient is assumed.

**The Specht and reverse-standard simple comparisons.** The evaluation maps have $x_j=m+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$, so [F2] makes each evaluated Specht factor self-dual. Twisting its reflected evaluation by $\sigma$ changes $-m$ to $m$ and every Jucys transposition to its sign twist. Ordinary conjugate-Specht/sign duality, followed by the reversed-induction isomorphism of step 1.5, gives $\sigma^*S(A^t)=S(A)^\circledast$. For $A\in\mathrm{Rev}$ put $B=A^\downarrow$. The actual tilting bottom flag gives an embedding $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)=P(B)$, hence $S(A)\hookrightarrow Y(B)$ by exactness. The symmetric trace identifies a primitive projective cover $He$ with $(eH)^*$; since $Z\mapsto eZ$ is exact, this is the injective hull of its split simple top, with unique essential socle $D(B)$. Every nonzero submodule therefore contains that socle, giving $\operatorname{soc}S(A)=D(B)$. Duality converts it to the simple head of $S(A)^\circledast$. Since $A^t$ is standard, the target standard-head statement and exact sign pullback now give $\sigma^*D(A^t)=D(A^\downarrow)$. No arbitrary quotient is assumed to preserve a head or socle.

**The full Young generator algebra.** For every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ put $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A):=\pi P_{\mathcal O}(A)$; by step 1.3 full faithfulness on projectives makes these nonzero indecomposable with local endomorphism rings, and makes them pairwise nonisomorphic, while for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ they are the projective covers $Y(A)$ of [F1]. If some $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ were projective, it would be a sum of standard projective covers, and full faithfulness on the distinct O-projectives $P_{\mathcal O}(A)$ would give an identification of two nonisomorphic O-projectives, a contradiction; so off-standard images are nonprojective. Taking the full finite sum $Y_{\mathrm{all}}=\bigoplus_{A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda}Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ (one representative each) and using full faithfulness on the corresponding full projective generator $Q=\bigoplus_AP_{\mathcal O}(A)$ gives $\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$, the quasihereditary Schur-cover algebra of [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]] and [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]. Summing only the standard projective covers would give a Morita generator of $H^\Lambda$, which is symmetric and not quasihereditary in general, and is not the algebra meant here.

**An explicit trace-adjoint covector.** Positions have nonincreasing original column types $t_1\ge\cdots\ge t_d$, constant inside exterior blocks $J$. Put $p=\prod_j\prod_{i<t_j}(x_j-m_i)$, $a_-=\sum_{u\in J}\operatorname{sgn}(u)u$ and $g=pa_-=a_-p=g^*$. The native right dot formula on row tensors of columns $c_j$ is $vx_j=v_{L_j}+m_{c_j}v+\sum_{h<j,c_h\ge c_j}v(hj)-\sum_{h>j,c_h<c_j}v(jh)$. At that stage the target columns are $t_h$ for $h<j$, $i$ at $j$, and one for $h>j$. Transposing the dot formula has no earlier swap, since $t_h\ge t_j>i$, and no later swap, since $1\le i$; its diagonal is $m_i-m_i=0$. **The signed full generator and Ringel duality.** Likewise put $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A):=\pi T_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$. Full faithfulness on tiltings (step 1.3) makes the full sum $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}=\bigoplus_A\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ satisfy $\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(\bigoplus_AT_{\mathcal O}(A))^{op}$, and the characteristic-tilting endomorphism algebra is the Ringel dual of the Schur-cover algebra, realized as the reversed-Levi/opposite-parabolic block via the functor $F=D\Psi$ with its explicit reverse-column shifts and $F(\overline P(A))=T_{\mathcal O}(A)$, by [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]], [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]] and [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]. For a proper original lower ideal the opposite datum is the matching highest-weight Serre quotient, not the same downset subcategory, and no unqualified longest-Borel twisting equivalence on all of $\mathcal O$ is used. Positive finite multiplicities replace the generator by a Morita-equivalent one with the same module category.

**The exact ideal kernel.** The top PBW trace $\tau$ equals $\phi_0\mathrm{reg}$: only the bounded monomial with all exponents $l-1$ and identity permutation reaches the all-column-one fixed-order tensor in top degree. Consequently $\tau(bg)=\lambda(q\,\mathrm{reg}(b))$. If $b\in K$, every $ab\in K$ and $\tau(abg)=0$ for all $a$, so nondegeneracy gives $bg=0$. Hence $H/K\to Hg$, $b+K\mapsto bg$, is well defined and surjective. The exterior row basis has size $(d!/|J|)\prod_j(l-t_j+1)$. In the truncated polynomial/permutation associated graded, with $b_j=t_j-1$, the words $uX^{\mathbf r+\mathbf b}a_-$, $u\in S_d/J$, $0\le r_j\le l-t_j$, are independent: different cosets have disjoint permutation supports and different exponent vectors have different polynomial supports. Their filtered lifts give that many independent vectors in $Hg$. Dimension comparison proves $K=\operatorname{Ann}_{\rm left}(g)$ and $H/K\cong Hg$. The bare trace adjoint has RIGHT image $gH$; applying the generator-fixing anti-involution gives the contragredient LEFT image $Hg$.
All roots may repeat, since none was divided by a difference.

**Lifting the kernel in category $\mathcal O$.** Let $T=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(I^\Lambda\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ and $E(A)=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(I^\Lambda\otimes D_0)$, with the ordinary ground $I^\Lambda$ and the exterior suffix factor $D_0$ above. Exact parabolic induction supplies $q:T\twoheadrightarrow E(A)$. Natural finite-W transport and regular evaluation identify $\pi(q)$ with the preceding exterior quotient and $\pi(R_g)$ with right multiplication by $g$. A finite total-column-degree filtration makes the nilradical act trivially on its graded finite Levi pieces; complete reducibility refines this to a standard flag of $E(A)$. The projective $T$ also has a standard flag. Any simple submodule of either object injects into its first nonzero standard section and so has standard label by [F3]. Therefore $\pi$ detects nonzero SUBMODULES of these two objects, without being conservative on the whole category. Since $\pi(R_g\ker q)=0$, detection gives $R_g\ker q=0$. Thus $R_g$ factors as $Fq$ with $F:E(A)\to T$. Its Schur image is the injective map $H/K\to Hg\subset H$; detection on submodules of $E(A)$ makes $F$ injective. Hence $\ker q=\ker R_g$ as actual category-$\mathcal O$ submodules.

**A genuine tilting module, not just its character.** The ground restricted form times the natural tensor dot product gives a symmetric nondegenerate contravariant form $B_T$; Casimir and place permutations are self-adjoint, hence so is $g$. The form $B_E(qt,qu)=B_T(t,R_gu)$ is well defined by the actual kernel equality of step 4.1. If $qt$ is in its radical, self-adjointness and nondegeneracy of $B_T$ force $R_gt=0$, hence $qt=0$. It is symmetric and contravariant, and finite weight spaces make it a perfect restricted form. Thus $E(A)$ is self-dual. Dualizing its already established standard flag gives a costandard flag, so it is a tilting object; arbitrary parabolic induction has not been asserted to preserve tiltings.

**The leading tilting summand.** For a product of wedges with lengths $\nu_s$, occupation of the first $r$ coordinates is at most $\sum_s\min(r,\nu_s)=\sum_{a\le r}\lambda_a$. Equality at the highest weight forces every wedge of length at least $a$ to contain its $a$th initial coordinate; that tensor is unique. In a suffix allocation, slots can move only to later Levi blocks. If $u_{<j}$ slots originally before $j$ move to block $j$ or later, the degree before $j$ drops by $u_{<j}$, while at most $u_{<j}$ moved slots can increase the first $r$ coordinates in block $j$. Thus every resulting highest partition $\beta$ satisfies $\sum_{i<j}|\beta^{(i)}|+\sum_{a\le r}\beta_a^{(j)}\le\sum_{i<j}|\lambda^{(i)}|+\sum_{a\le r}\lambda_a^{(j)}$. Any moved slot gives a strict component boundary; equality everywhere forces the unique original leading tensor. Exact induction consequently gives $[E(A):M(A)]=1$ with all other standards strictly lower in multipartition dominance.

Tilting classification and its leading-standard triangularity then yield $E(A)=T(A)\oplus\bigoplus_{\lambda(B)<\lambda(A)}T(B)^{\oplus m_B}$. This is an actual tilting decomposition obtained after step 5.1, not a module isomorphism inferred from characters alone.

**Ordinary and signed Young extraction on ALL labels.** The ordinary cumulative-column symmetric-power objects in the full-projective copresentation proof are genuine projectives. Schur-Weyl and Specht-to-permutation dominance give their leading standard $M(A)$ once and only multipartitions strictly above $\lambda(A)$ otherwise. BGG projective triangularity therefore gives $P(A)$ once and only projectives of higher multipartition dominance. For the ordinary component types $t_1\le\cdots\le t_d$, put $p_+=\prod_j\prod_{i>t_j}(x_j-m_i)$ and let $a_+$ sum the within-row Young subgroup $J_+$. Acting on the rightmost regular tensor $w$, process $j$ from left to right and the factors at position $j$ from $i=l$ down to $t_j+1$. Earlier positions already have columns $t_h\le t_j<i$, while later ones remain in column $l\ge i$, so the native dot formula has no spectator swaps; subtracting $m_i$ leaves exactly the next left shift. Thus $wp_+$ is exactly the nondecreasing-column tensor, and $wp_+a_+$ is its within-block symmetric sum.

It belongs to the actual cumulative-column symmetric submodule $e_SZ(A)$. The map $Hp_+a_+\to e_SZ(A)$ induced by regular evaluation is injective. Its target has dimension $(d!/|J_+|)\prod_j t_j$. In the associated graded algebra the coset words $uX^{\mathbf r+\mathbf b}a_+$ with $b_j=l-t_j$, $0\le r_j<t_j$, have disjoint polynomial/permutation supports and are independent. Hence the source has at least the target dimension and is exactly that submodule. This proves $\pi Z(A)=Hp_+a_+$ locally. Under reversed transpose, the reflected charges satisfy $m_i^t=-m_{l+1-i}$. Applying $\sigma$ to the displayed ordinary product sends each factor to a unit $-1$ times $(x_j-m_i)$, and the ordinary symmetrizer becomes $a_-$. Its positional bounds become $t_1\ge\cdots\ge t_d$ and its factors exactly $i<t_j$, so its left ideal is precisely $Hg_A$ from step 2.3; transpose reverses multipartition dominance. Consequently the signed module $Hg_A$ has the triangular decomposition with leading $\sigma^*Y_{\rm all}(A^t)$ once and strictly lower terms.

Steps 3.4 and 6.2 give the SAME family of signed modules a triangular decomposition with leading $\pi T(A)$ once and strictly lower terms. Full faithfulness on projectives and tiltings makes both leading families nonzero indecomposable, pairwise nonisomorphic, with local endomorphism rings. Induction upwards from minimal multipartition labels and Krull-Schmidt cancellation identifies the two leading summands at every label, proving $\pi T(A)\cong\sigma^*Y_{\rm all}(A^t)$ for ALL column-strict labels. It is not inferred only for standard labels.

**Blocks, cuts and the requested consequences.** Every map, form and kernel above commutes with central block projection; the block trace is nondegenerate. Auxiliary ground-row deletion selects the original row names and preserves the forbidden-column and exterior relations, so the natural quotient maps agree with the accepted admissible central-corner transfer. Thus the full-label comparison survives the admitted finite chunks and the reflected global cuts. On reverse-standard labels step 2.1 makes the signed image the projective cover $Y(A^\downarrow)$. The full generator endomorphism algebras are precisely those identified in steps 2.2 and 3.2; positive finite multiplicities change only the Morita generator. The claimed source self-duality follows from the restricted forms and the duality-compatible Schur quotient.

**Domains.** The global sign statement lives on $I=\mathbb Z$ and on reflected auxiliary finite cuts realizing it, chosen with every charge inside the root interval; its categorical realization uses the finite bounded chunks of the bounded-chunk construction above, not a simultaneously bounded-below index set preserved by negation, and the bounded chunks realize the sign comparison through the finite double-cut identifications of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]. The two domains, global label reversal and finite-chunk categorical duality, are thus kept distinct.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 gives the sign isomorphism and the residue intertwining $i\leftrightarrow-i$; steps 1.2 and 2.1 give the transpose bijection and the Specht/simple comparison with the rectified labels; step 3.1 gives the parameter-one descent to the projected lattices; steps 2.2-3.2 identify the full Young and signed generators with the Schur-cover algebra and its Ringel dual, including the off-standard nonprojectivity and the opposite-parabolic/serre-quotient clauses; step 8.1 gives the signed-Young comparison; and step 9.1 separates the global and bounded-chunk domains. No unqualified twisting equivalence and no off-standard simple label is used.

Use the actual source chart at parameter $s$: with the monomials $M_A$ and the
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$ of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], put

$$R_{A,B}(s)=p_{A,B}(-s),\qquad L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A,\qquad M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A . $$

Thus $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ is the INVERSE of $R(s)$, not its transpose. Also
$P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$.

**(i)** For every Specht label $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ and every simple label
$A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $[S(B):D(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$.

**(ii)** In the usual Specht-row/simple-column notation the rectangular
decomposition matrix is the transpose of $D$ restricted to standard rows; it is
NOT the transpose of the $L$-in-$M$ chart. The full matrix $D$ is unitriangular
on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, and its square submatrix on standard columns is
unitriangular; in particular $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ only for
$B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, since for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the object
$D(B)=0$ is not a simple module label.

**(iii)** Retain the type-$A$ polynomial formula: for the right place action,
$w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the ENTRY stabilizer $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, and

$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}),$$

while the COLUMN Levi $J$ is a distinct group; the mixed singular/parabolic
composition matrix is the finite Levi cancellation sum over $C$ column-equivalent
to $B$, $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$, and equals
$d_{A,B}(1)$. All categorification multiplicities are ungraded at parameter
one, with the source/library reciprocal convention.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$. Then the two identifications of the preceding

$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,

derivations.claim: **The four monomials and the label sets.** For $I=\{0\}$ the admissible letters are $0$ and the shifted letter $1$, level two gives the two fundamental tensor factors, and the tenable monomials of $V\otimes V$ in the two-factor window are $00,01,10,11$; a bipartition $(a;b)$ with $a+b\le2$ has column-strict tableaux with entries $0\le$ entries and row-weak inequalities exactly for $ab=00,01,11$, while $10$ is column-strict but reverse-standard, so $\mathrm{Std}=\{00,01,11\}$ and $\mathrm{Rev}=\{00,10,11\}$; the Bruhat order on the two-entry column has $01<10$. The weight of a monomial is the sum of its entries, giving $\mathrm{wt}(00)=0$, $\mathrm{wt}(01)=\mathrm{wt}(10)=\alpha_0$, $\mathrm{wt}(11)=2\alpha_0$, so the tower degrees are $0,1,2$ and $I_{\alpha_0}=\{(0,1),(1,0)\}$.

**The transition vectors.** On the mixed two-dimensional weight space the ordinary Fock bar satisfies $\psi M_{10}=M_{10}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{01}$ and fixes the other three monomials, so the triangularity conditions $L_B=M_B+\sum_{C<B}s\mathbb Z[s]M_C$ give $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$ and $L_{00}=M_{00}$, $L_{01}=M_{01}$, $L_{11}=M_{11}$; the canonical family is $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$, and the quasi-canonical vector is $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}=sT_{10}$. Inverting the triangular matrix gives $M_{10}=L_{10}+sL_{01}$, so the ambient $d$-matrix has $d_{01,10}=s$ and is the inverse of the $L$-in-$M$ chart, not its transpose.

**The normalized projection.** The kernel of the normalized highest projection $\pi$ is spanned by the off-standard vectors $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$, and $\pi$ is the unique projection with $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle$-normalization $\pi P=0$ for odd vectors and $\pi M_{A_\Lambda}=M_{A_\Lambda}$; on the mixed space the highest vector is $M_{01}$ with $E_0M_{01}=M_{00}$ and $E_0T_{10}=(s+s^{-1})M_{00}$, so the normalization forces $D_{01}=\pi L_{01}=\pi(T_{10}/(s+s^{-1}))=T_{10}/(s+s^{-1})$ and $\pi M_{10}=\pi(M_{10}-L_{10})=s\pi L_{01}=sD_{01}$, while $\pi L_{10}=0$; the endpoints are $D_{00}=M_{00}$ and $D_{11}=M_{11}$, and at parameter one $D_{01}=(M_{01}+M_{10})/2$. **The supported blocks.** Set $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$. The defining relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$ and $x^2=0$ in the relevant degree; from $ux^2=0$ and the cross relations one obtains $y^2u=x+y$, hence $y^2=(x+y)u$, and reducing the relation $y^2=(x+y)u$ decreases the $y$-exponent while killing $x$-exponents at least $2$, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-$2$ algebra. Then $[P_i]$ and $[S_i]$ are $R=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, respectively, and $$\langle[P_i],[S_j]\rangle_{A,\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{cases}\dim_k\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i),&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j.\end{cases}$$ If $\operatorname{End}_{A,0}(S_i)=k$ for every representative, these Laurent bases are dual. finite-dimensional projective left $A$-module $P$ and finite-dimensional left
$A$-module $M$, define the object-level value

$$h(P,M):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,M).$$

If $A$ is $\mathbb Z$-graded and $P,M$ are finite-dimensional graded left $A$-modules,

$$h_{\mathrm{gr}}(P,M):=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}v^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,M),$$

derivations.claim: **The degree-one block.** For $I=\{0\}$, level $2$ and charge $(0,0)$ the degree-one cyclotomic quotient is $H^{(0,0)}_1=\mathbb C[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ by the level-two instance of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], and it is already supported, so $B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ with $x=x_1$. Its radical is $(x)$ and its quotient is $\mathbb C$, so $B$ is local; the unique simple is $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ with $x\mapsto0$, the regular module $Y_{01}=B$ is its projective cover, and the regular composition series $0\subset(x)\subset B$ has successive quotients $D_{01},D_{01}$, giving $[Y_{01}]=2[D_{01}]$ in $G_0$. Every $B$-linear map $B\to D_{01}$ is determined by the image of $1$, so $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{01},D_{01})=1$.

**The symmetric form on $B$ and self-duality.** The coefficient functional $\tau(a+bx)=b$ is a symmetrizing trace on $B$: it is linear, $\tau(uv)=\tau(vu)$ for all $u,v$ (both sides pick out the $x$-coefficient of the product), and its radical is zero because $\tau(x)\ne0$, so the associated form $\langle u,v\rangle=\tau(uv)$ has matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ in the basis $(1,x)$, which is nonsingular. The anti-involution $\ast$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] that fixes $x$ is the identity of $B$ here, so the form is generator-fixing, and it exhibits an isomorphism $Y_{01}\cong Y_{01}^{\circledast}$: the dual of the regular module with respect to the trace. This is the actual symmetric-algebra proof of cover self-duality, not an inference from self-duality of the head.

**The degree-two block and its simple.** With $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$ the relations give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$, $x^2=0$, and from $ux^2=0$ one gets $y^2=(x+y)u$, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-two algebra; the models $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ and $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ satisfy all relations, and the central Hermite projectors of the element $z=x+y$ separate the three factors, which proves that the span of the eight words is isomorphic to $M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$. The supported content cut at $2\alpha_0$ keeps the factor $M_2(\mathbb C)$; its simple module $\mathbb C^2$ has Gram matrix $J$, since $N^{t}J=JN$ and $(-J)^{t}J=J(-J)$, and it is self-dual and projective, so its projective cover is itself and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$; degree $0$ contributes $\mathbb C$, and Hom-spaces between distinct content blocks vanish because they are different blocks. In particular the one-dimensional Fock weight vector $M_{11}$ is not the two-dimensional module $D_{11}$, and the composition length of the degree-two projective cover is $2$, not $1$.

**The projected dual bases at parameter one.** By [F1] the categorification images are the projected vectors; on the mixed weight the normalized highest vector is $P_{01}=M_{01}+M_{10}$ of $C_0$-norm $2$, so the correct field dual is $D_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$, and the endpoint vectors satisfy $P_{00}=D_{00}=M_{00}$ and $P_{11}=D_{11}=M_{11}$. The Gram matrix in the $D$-basis is $\operatorname{diag}(1,\tfrac12,1)$ and the change of basis $\operatorname{diag}(1,2,1)$ converts it into the identity, which is the pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; this is the parameter-one projected-simple dictionary of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]], not an identification of $L_{01}=M_{01}$ with the simple.

**The categorified residue operators.** Induction from degree $0$ to the degree-one block gives the regular module of $B$; the supported induction from $B$ to the degree-two block $M_2(\mathbb C)$ sends the simple $\mathbb C$ to $\mathbb C^2$ and the regular module $B$ to $M_2(\mathbb C)$, which is two copies of the simple $\mathbb C^2$; restriction of $\mathbb C^2$ to $B$ is the regular Jordan module $B$ itself (the generator $x$ of $B$ acts on $\mathbb C^2$ as $N$ with $N^2=0$ and $\dim\ker N=1$), and restriction of $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ is the simple $B$-module. Using the exact residue functors of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]] and the categorification identification of [F1], this yields the displayed columns $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$, $fD_{11}=0$ and $eD_{00}=0$, $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$; equivalently, in the $D$-basis, $f$ has columns $(0,2,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,0,1)^{\mathsf T},0$ and $e$ has columns $0,(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T},(0,2,0)^{\mathsf T}$, so the commutator is $\operatorname{diag}(2,0,-2)$ in the $sl_2$-normalization of [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]].

**The index-two lattice and its cyclicity.** The divided powers $f^{(2)}=f^2/2$ and $e^{(2)}=e^2/2$ give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$, and the displayed operators multiply $D_{01}$-coordinates by even integers, so the lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$, their divided powers and the toral operators at weights $2,0,-2$. This proves that integral costandard generation fails while the full integral duality and the standard divided-power statement survive.

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$
(equivalently $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$);

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of
$\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$;

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
$D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$);

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being the rectification
$A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ and its inverse $\downarrow$ between
$\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks,
intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible

$\alpha=0$ and the ground survive.

The theorem of this page is the *degenerate* Ariki categorification theorem
([[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]): it concerns the tower
$H^\Lambda$ over $\mathbb C$ built from the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras
at an integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$
([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]), and it identifies the two
Grothendieck groups at parameter one with the type-$A$ Fock/highest weight data
of $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$.

It neither states nor implies the categorification theorem for the
nondegenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebras $H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ at a Hecke
parameter $\xi$: the only bridge recorded here is the isomorphism
$H^\Lambda_d\cong H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ for $\xi$ *not* a root of unity (generic
$\xi$), which is not available at roots of unity. At a root of unity of order
$e$ the nondegenerate theory is a different theorem, stated for the affine type
$A^{(1)}_{e-1}$ Fock space with residues modulo $e$ and graded
(canonical-basis) coefficients, supplied by the cyclotomic KLR algebras and the
Hecke-KLR isomorphism, not by this page. In particular no coefficient computed
here determines the root-of-unity graded decomposition data, and the
congruence $H^\Lambda_d\cong H^\Lambda_{\xi,d}$ at generic $\xi$ must not be
specialized. The generic parameter dictionary is $(T_r-\xi)(T_r+1)=0$ with
cyclotomic roots $Q_j=\xi^{m_j}$ on the nondegenerate side and roots $m_j$ on
the degenerate side; the algebra isomorphism is not literal equality of $x_r$
and $X_r$. The claimed failure is of universal root-parameter transport:
particular accidental root-parameter isomorphisms do not supply it.

derivations.claim: **The available bridge and its limit.** By [F2] the only recorded comparison between the two settings is the isomorphism over a characteristic-zero field between the cyclotomic Hecke algebra at $q$ not a root of unity and its rational degeneration $q=1$; the source notes that Ariki's theorem for generic $q$ is thereby equivalent to the degenerate theorem. That statement is an algebra isomorphism in the generic regime and does not extend to specializations: at a root of unity no such isomorphism is asserted, so the proposed transport step is not available.

**The level-one obstruction at $\xi=-1$.** By [F1] the generic type-$A$ Hecke algebra has the quadratic relation $T^2=(\xi-1)T+\xi$, so at $\xi=-1$ the specialization over $\mathbb C$ is $\mathbb C[T]/(T^2-(-2)T-1)=\mathbb C[T]/((T+1)^2)$: a two-dimensional commutative algebra whose element $T+1$ is nonzero and squares to zero, with a nonzero radical and exactly one simple module. The degenerate level-one quotient is $H_d(a)=\mathbb C[S_d]$; at $d=2$ and any charge this is $\mathbb C[S_2]=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, semisimple with two simple modules. The two algebras are not isomorphic, because an isomorphism of unital algebras preserves the nilpotence of the radical and the number of simple modules; hence the degenerate level-one decomposition data, which is trivial, cannot determine the nondegenerate root-of-unity data. This computation uses the whole two-dimensional algebras, not the supported degree-two cut of the tower.

**The scope mismatch at a root of unity of order $e$.** By [F2] at a primitive $e$-th root of unity the nondegenerate theory replaces the rational degeneration by the sign-modified cyclotomic KLR algebra of affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$ for $e>0$ (and type $A_\infty$ for $e=0$), with residues taken modulo $e$ and with graded canonical-basis coefficients; the quantum characteristic $e$ and the grading do not occur in the degenerate statement at all. Therefore no statement on this page supplies the nondegenerate theorem at a root of unity, even before the obstruction of step 2.1, and the generic comparison cannot be specialized.

**Conclusion.** The proposed implication asserts transport of the degenerate theorem to every nondegenerate parameter. Step 1.1 shows that the only available bridge is the generic isomorphism; step 2.1 exhibits the concrete level-one failure at $\xi=-1$ by comparing the full two-dimensional algebras, so the implication already fails at level one; and step 3.1 records the root-of-unity scope mismatch. The genuine generic equivalence and the true further results comparing the theories at roots of unity are retained as sourced statements; what is refuted is only the universal root-parameter transport. If a finite root interval is used for a specialization comparison, it must be enlarged to include the values determining the algebra, such as $m-1$ and $m+1$ in place of a supported cut $I=\{m\}$; accidental isomorphisms at particular root parameters do not supply the claimed implication.

derivations.claim: **The eight ambient labels.** By the multipartition dictionary each bipartition of total size at most two corresponds to a column-strict tableau of the two-column window: the empty bipartition gives $00=OO$; the two size-one bipartitions give $01=OU$ and $10=UO$; the three size-two bipartitions give $11=UU$, the vertical $C0$ whose first component is empty and whose second is $(1,1)$, and the remaining ones; translating by the ground-difference rule at charge $(0,0)$ gives precisely the eight columns $OO,OU,UO,UU,OR,RO,OC,CO$ listed, including the vertical column $C=(1,0,-2,-3,\dots)$ whose top entry alone would not record its size two. The root degrees are computed from the entry differences: $00$ has degree $0$; $01$ and $10$ have degree $\alpha_0$; $11$ has degree $2\alpha_0$; $0R,R0$ have degree $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$; and $0C,C0$ have degree $\alpha_0+\alpha_{-1}$. Strict columns plus weak row inequalities define $\mathrm{Std}=\{00,01,11,0R,0C\}$, the reversed inequalities define $\mathrm{Rev}=\{00,10,11,R0,C0\}$, and the unique weight-preserving matching in the ground component is the rectification $10\mapsto01$, $R0\mapsto0R$, $C0\mapsto0C$ with $00,11$ fixed.

**The full height-two window.** With $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$ the relations give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$ and $x^2=0$; from $ux^2=0$ one derives $y^2=(x+y)u$, and reducing by this relation decreases the $y$-exponent while killing $x$-exponents at least two, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-two algebra. The three models $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ on $B_+$, and $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $B_-$ satisfy the relations by direct matrix computation; the central element $z=x+y$ has images $0$, $1+2\epsilon$ and $-1+2\epsilon$, and the Hermite polynomials $E_0=(1-z^2)^2$, $E_\pm=(1-E_0\pm(3z-z^3)/2)/2$ map to the three separate identities.
